concerns.description: Significant text omission within a section
concerns.analysis: On page 16, under section 'f) iii)', there is a significant omission. The source PDF contains three substantive paragraphs numbered (1), (a), and (b) detailing security policies and encryption requirements. The output completely misses these paragraphs, replacing them with extraction artifacts ('null').
concerns.source_pdf_quote: (1) Any NCDIT security policy regarding Cloud Computing, and the NCDIT Statewide Information Security Policy Manual, to include encryption requirements as defined below: (a) The Contractor shall encrypt all non-public data in transit regardless of the transit mechanism. (b) For engagements where the Contractor stores sensitive personally identifiable or otherwise confidential information, this data shall be encrypted at rest.
concerns.output_quote: iii) That the Services will comply with the following:null, to include encryption requirements as defined below:null

concerns.analysis: On page 126, there is a catastrophic structural failure where internal JSON formatting leaked into the text field itself. This collapses multiple paragraphs, lists, and headings (including the 'POSTAGE METER RENTAL AGREEMENT' heading and its subsequent list items) into a single continuous literal string containing JSON syntax. This completely breaks the reading order and semantic structure of the content for the remainder of the page.

concerns.analysis: standalone_links=71, examples=['https://eprocurement.nc.gov', 'https://eprocurement.nc.gov/', 'https://it.nc.gov/document/statewide-data-classification-and']. Links should be inline within paragraphs, not separate blocks.

concerns.analysis: bare_url_count=5. URLs appear as plain text instead of clickable links.

concerns.description: Table cells contain 11 unlinked URL(s)/email(s) that should be hyperlinks
concerns.analysis: bare_urls_in_tables=11. Examples: p2: r.mikel@quadient.com; p2: r.mikel@quadient.com; p2: k.warner@quadient.com. URLs and emails in table cells should be clickable links.

concerns.description: List numbering restart(s): 10 ordered list(s) restart numbering at 1 instead of continuing sequence
concerns.analysis: restart_count=10. Examples: p2: heading "4. Participating Entity Modifications or"; p7: list restarts at 1 (prev page 6 ended at 4); p12: 2 single-item ordered lists (fragmented). Ordered lists that restart numbering suggest content was split across page breaks and not reassembled.

concerns.description: Form elements detected: 6 form(s) with 29 field(s) — forms lose functionality in HTML
concerns.analysis: form_count=6, total_fields=29. PDF form fields (checkboxes, text inputs, signatures) cannot be faithfully rendered as static HTML.

concerns.description: Links displaced to end of page: 11 link(s) clustered at bottom of 5 page(s) instead of inline in text
concerns.analysis: displaced_link_pages=5, total_displaced=11. Links appear as standalone elements at the end of pages rather than being inline in the paragraph text.

The source PDF frequently uses underlining to emphasize terms at the beginning of list items (e.g., 'Worker's Compensation' and 'Commercial General Liability' on page 10). This structural emphasis is completely lost in the JSON output, which lacks any underline notation for these phrases.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: i. Worker’s Compensation - The Contractor shall provide...
concerns.output_quote: "text": "i. Worker’s Compensation - The Contractor shall provide and maintain Worker’s Compensation Insurance..."

concerns.description: Header/footer elements retained in output (188): Participating Addendum - Master Agreement CTR058809 – Quadie; Participating Addendum - Master Agreement CTR058809 – Quadie; Participating Addendum - Master Agreement CTR058809 - Quadie
concerns.analysis: header_footer_count=188. Header/footer elements are present in extraction data. This is common in multi-page government PDFs and is typically cosmetic — the renderer strips them from HTML output.

concerns.description: Mixed numbering types at same list level (1 list(s)): p117:letter+numeric — possible sub-point flattening
concerns.analysis: flat_lists=1. Lists with mixed numbering types (numeric+letter or numeric+roman) at the same depth level suggest sub-points were flattened.

concerns.description: Numbered items as headings: 13 heading(s) look like numbered list items
concerns.analysis: heading_list_count=13. Headings starting with '1.', '2.' etc. suggest numbered list items were misclassified as headings during extraction.
